findings.claim: The change defines `self.downsize` twice. Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the first `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Every caller using the old 5-argument form now raises ArgumentError, so custom emoji resizing breaks silently in Sidekiq.
findings.evidence: app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which is 5 arguments to a method that takes 3..4. The job is enqueued from app/models/emoji.rb:73. There is no ResizeEmoji spec, and optimized_image_spec stubs `resize`, so the suite will not catch this. Repros (reasoned, not run): `ruby -wc app/models/optimized_image.rb` should warn 'method redefined; discarding old downsize'. `ruby -e 'class A; def self.d(f,t,w,h,o={});end; def self.d(f,t,dim,o={});end;end; A.d(1,2,100,100,{})'` should raise ArgumentError. `Jobs::ResizeEmoji.new.execute(path: "spec/fixtures/images/logo.png")` should raise ArgumentError.
findings.reason: Four seats agree, and every seat cites the same caller. Candidate red test: a Jobs::ResizeEmoji spec that runs the job and expects no ArgumentError. Ponytail's suggested fix: delete lines 145-147 and change resize_emoji.rb:14 to pass "100x100".

verifier.reason: The patch adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at app/models/optimized_image.rb:149, which replaces the 5-argument version at line 145. app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments, and that job is enqueued from app/models/emoji.rb:73, so the call raises ArgumentError.

findings.claim: The client-side size check replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` for every upload type. Attachments between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10 MB now pass in the browser and are then rejected by the server. Sites with limits above 10240 KB are capped by a limit the admin never set. Only images needed the limit relaxed.
findings.evidence: The server still enforces `max_#{type}_size_kb` in lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-86, and upload-selector.js.es6:17 still reads `max_attachment_size_kb`. Existing QUnit test test/javascripts/lib/utilities-test.js.es6:52-61 ('prevents files that are too big from being uploaded') sets max_image_size_kb=5, uploads a 10 KB image and expects rejection with max_size_kb: 5. On the patched code validUpload returns true (reasoned; run with `rake qunit:test`).
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Normalised to Important: three seats rated it Important and ponytail rated it Minor. Candidate red test: the existing QUnit test above, plus a QUnit attachment case with max_attachment_size_kb=1 and a 2 KB file. Fix together with the 10 MB constants at utilities.js:246 and uploads_controller.rb:55.

verifier.reason: The patch changes utilities.js:182 so the browser size check uses a hardcoded 10*1024 KB for every upload type instead of `max_<type>_size_kb`. The server still checks `max_#{type}_size_kb` (lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81-85) and only images get downsized by the new uploads_controller loop, so attachments above the admin's limit now pass in the browser and are rejected by the server, and limits above 10 MB are capped in the browser.

findings.claim: The HTTP 413 handler now always tells the user the limit is 10240 KB. A 413 comes from nginx or another proxy, whose limit is whatever the operator configured, so the message misstates the real limit on many installs.
findings.evidence: This is shown by the diff line itself. The 10m in config/nginx.sample.conf:61 is only a sample default. All seats reasoned this; none ran it.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Normalised to Important: mattpocock and superpowers rated it Important, open-code-review grouped it under an Important finding, and ponytail rated it Minor. Candidate red test: a QUnit test of the 413 error path with a non-10240 setting that asserts the reported max_size_kb.

verifier.reason: The patch changes utilities.js:246 so the 413 handler always reports a fixed `10 * 1024` KB limit. A 413 comes from the proxy, and that limit is set per install: config/nginx.sample.conf:61 uses 10m but docs/INSTALL-ubuntu.md:390 shows 2m. Before the patch the handler showed max_image_size_kb, which the setting descriptions (e.g. server.en.yml:1037) tell operators to keep in sync with client_max_body_size.

findings.claim: The API URL-download cap changed from `max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, regardless of type or site settings. It duplicates the nginx `client_max_body_size 10m` in a third place with no setting behind it. On sites with limits above 10 MB, larger API URL uploads are truncated rather than cleanly rejected.
findings.evidence: This is shown by the diff line. `FileHelper.download` stops reading once the file passes max_file_size (open-code-review, superpowers). Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Four seats agree. Normalised to Minor: three seats rated it Minor and mattpocock rated it Important. It shares a root cause with utilities.js:182/246, so the same change should fix it. No red test is required at Minor.

verifier.reason: The patch changes app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`, and lib/file_helper.rb:18 stops reading once the file passes that size without raising an error. On a site with a limit above 10 MB, a larger file is cut to about 10.5 MB, which is under the limit, so the UploadValidator check (lib/validators/upload_validator.rb:81) accepts it and the cut-off file gets stored.

findings.claim: With `allow_animated_thumbnails` on, an oversized GIF is routed to `downsize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects a WxH geometry, so gifsicle should exit non-zero and `convert_with` returns false. The loop then burns all 5 attempts and the upload is still rejected.
findings.evidence: optimized_image.rb:113-122 builds the gifsicle command. The claim rests on gifsicle CLI syntax and was not executed by any seat.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Normalised to Important: mattpocock and superpowers rated it Important and open-code-review rated it Minor. Unverified: no seat ran gifsicle. Step 5 needs a red repro, such as running `gifsicle --resize-fit 80% in.gif -o out.gif` and asserting a non-zero exit, or a controller spec with an oversized GIF. If that cannot be made red, defer it marked unverified.

verifier.reason: The new loop at uploads_controller.rb:62-46 (patch lines 41-46) calls OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: ...). For a path ending in .GIF, optimized_image.rb:155 sends it to downsize_instructions_animated, which builds `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%` (optimized_image.rb:115-123,137-139). --resize-fit takes a WxH geometry, so gifsicle errors, convert_with returns false (161-162), the size never shrinks, and all 5 attempts run before the upload is rejected. I did not run gifsicle; this relies on its documented syntax. The .gif path is certain for API URL uploads, because FileHelper.download keeps the extension (file_helper.rb:13-14).

findings.claim: With `allow_animated_thumbnails` off, `convert #{from}[0]` writes only the first frame back over the original, so an oversized animated GIF silently becomes a static image.
findings.evidence: This is reasoned from the downsize instructions. It was not run.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat, so it is not fixed in this loop. ponytail: animated GIF flattened to first frame when animated thumbnails are disabled.

findings.claim: The in-place downsize loop runs on a Tempfile, but image_optim replaces the file by rename, which creates a new inode. `tempfile.size` then fstats the stale descriptor. As a result all 5 iterations run (about 33% linear size), `Upload.create_for` gets a stale filesize, and FastImage dimensions and the sha1 can describe different bytes.
findings.evidence: This is reasoned. The image_optim `ImagePath#replace` rename behaviour was recalled from memory, not read. superpowers lists the same stale-handle question as not checked. Confirming test: a controller spec that uploads an oversized PNG and asserts `upload.filesize == File.size(stored_path)` and that the dimensions are 80% of the original.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat, so it is not fixed in this loop. Unverified: it depends on image_optim internals. ponytail: stale Tempfile size after rename-based ImageOptim replace.

findings.claim: The loop ignores the `downsize` return value and has no stop on failure. A failing conversion (bad image, convert error) is retried with the same command until all 5 attempts are used.
findings.evidence: This is shown by the loop body in the diff. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats, so it is not fixed in this loop. Normalised to Important (superpowers rated it Important, open-code-review Minor). ponytail: downsize failure not checked inside the retry loop.

findings.claim: Each upload can now trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick and ImageOptim runs on files of up to 10 MB. This raises latency and memory use, and for non-API uploads it stalls the shared Scheduler::Defer queue.
findings.evidence: superpowers cites uploads_controller.rb:19, where non-API uploads run in `Scheduler::Defer.later`. That corrects open-code-review's claim that the work runs synchronously in the web request; it does so only on the API path. mattpocock noted this concern but explicitly did not raise it. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats, so it is not fixed in this loop. Normalised to Important as a production risk. ponytail: synchronous multi-pass image processing on the upload path.

findings.claim: `FileHelper.is_image?` matches .svg, so an oversized SVG is run through `convert file.svg[0] -resize 80%\> file.svg`. That rewrites the user's SVG in place with ImageMagick output.
findings.evidence: Upload.create_for (upload.rb:63) and OptimizedImage.create_for (optimized_image.rb:44) both deliberately skip SVG. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one seat, so it is not fixed in this loop. ponytail: exclude SVG from the downsize loop.

findings.claim: The change has no tests. It adds a new downsize loop in the upload controller, changes OptimizedImage's public signatures and alters client-side validation, with zero spec or QUnit changes. That breaches the CONTRIBUTING rule 'Include tests'.
findings.evidence: The patch contains only 3 non-test files. The emoji breakage got through because nothing covers `downsize`.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by two seats, so it is not fixed in this loop. The red tests required in step 5 for the main-list fixes will add coverage for the touched paths. ponytail: add specs for the downsize loop.

findings.claim: The change removes the public `OptimizedImage.dimensions` and changes the signature of `optimize` without spec changes. Plugins calling either method would break.
findings.evidence: mattpocock and ponytail both grepped and found no other in-repo callers; ponytail calls the deletion correct. Only out-of-repo plugin breakage remains.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one advisory seat. The in-repo impact is disproved by both grep reports, but the plugin-API risk is not. ponytail: public API change to OptimizedImage.dimensions/optimize.

findings.claim: Two checks in the new guard do nothing. `tempfile.size > 0` adds nothing because the loop condition already fails for an empty file. `tempfile &&` protects nothing because line 72 dereferences `tempfile.size` anyway.
findings.evidence: This is shown by the guard and loop condition in the diff. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one advisory seat, so it is not fixed in this loop. ponytail: simplify guard to `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0 && FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`.

findings.reason: Appendix: raised by one advisory seat, so it is not fixed in this loop. ponytail: add a commit body when amending/squashing.
